feature_warmup: July 1-7 supplies the 168-hour lag; no July labels train the frozen models.

policy_comparison.fleet_selection_basis: Exploratory May 2026 sensitivity; July was not inspected for this choice.
policy_comparison.primary_outcome: traditional minus predictive mean response minutes after capped drain
policy_comparison.primary_unit: calendar day, averaged across paired seeds
policy_comparison.censoring_gate: Always report unanswered after drain and response completeness; if either policy has unresolved arrivals, the response mean is conditional and cannot alone establish superiority.
policy_comparison.stopping_rule: All 21 days and 10 paired seeds are required; no result-dependent stopping.

uncertainty.primary_interval: circular moving-block bootstrap of 21 daily paired means; block length 7 days, 10000 draws, seed 20261023
uncertainty.sensitivity_interval: same bootstrap with block length 3 days
uncertainty.secondary_test: HAC mean test with lag 3, asymptotic p value and 95% CI; interpretation conditional on stationarity/weak dependence
uncertainty.multiplicity: Holm across four prespecified secondary outcomes; no incident-level IID inference

observed_validation.comparison: Traditional simulated daily mean and P90 versus NYC EMS valid-response cohort, descriptive only

limitations: Model and simulator calibrated on April-June 2026; July is a new temporal window, not a new city or real dispatch trial.
July results cannot identify the effect of preventive relocation; neither policy relocates idle units.
The assumed fleet of 400 is not an observed FDNY inventory.
Twenty-one consecutive days give limited information about long-run seasonality and rare events.
Public source records can be corrected after extraction; archive and hash the snapshot used.
